title: Welcome
story:
A courier left a laptop at your door. No note, no sender, no explanation. The battery is at 4%. When the screen finally wakes up there is no desktop, no icons, no browser — just a blinking cursor waiting for you.

Someone wanted you to have this. Before you can find out who, you need to work out where you are.
objective: You are somewhere inside this machine, logged in as someone. Find out who you are and where you are standing.

tasks.description: Find out which user you are logged in as.
Find out which directory you are currently in.
There is a file waiting for you in your home directory. Read it.

hints.text: The cursor is a prompt — it is waiting for you to ask the machine a question. If you wanted to know who you were, what would you ask?
Linux commands are usually short, blunt English. There is a command whose entire job is to answer 'who am I?', and another that prints the directory you are working in.
Try `whoami` to see your username, then `pwd` to print your working directory. To read a file: `cat README.txt`.

knowledge.explanation: Every process on a Linux system runs as some user. That user decides what you are allowed to read, write and run. 'Who am I?' is not a philosophical question here — it is the first thing that determines what is possible.
knowledge.realWorld: Game: find out who you are → Security: establishing the security context of a session → Real world: the first question on any compromised host, because it tells an attacker what they already have and a defender whose account was used.

knowledge.explanation: The filesystem is a tree, and you are always standing somewhere in it. Commands you type act relative to where you stand, which is why the same command can behave differently in two places.
knowledge.realWorld: Game: print your directory → Security: filesystem orientation → Real world: knowing your position before acting is what separates deliberate work from guessing.

knowledge.explanation: A prompt is not a wall. You ask the machine a question, it answers, and the answer shapes your next question. Everything in this game is built on that loop.
knowledge.realWorld: Game: your first commands → Security: interactive investigation → Real world: every investigation, attack and incident response is this loop repeated.
